props.title: Hotel Rwanda

sections.content: Hotel Rwanda stands as one of cinema's most powerful depictions of both human cruelty and courage during genocide. Don Cheadle delivers a masterful performance as Paul Rusesabagina, the hotel manager who sheltered over 1,200 refugees during the Rwandan genocide. The film follows similar humanitarian crisis narratives like Schindler's List (1993) and The Killing Fields (1984), but director Terry George keeps the focus intensely personal, showing how ordinary people can become heroes in extraordinary circumstances.

sections.content: The film sparked renewed interest in African conflict cinema, paving the way for works like Blood Diamond (2006) and Beasts of No Nation (2015). These films share a commitment to exposing Western audiences to African realities while maintaining dramatic tension. The Last King of Scotland (2006) similarly used a compelling personal narrative to illuminate Uganda's brutal history under Idi Amin.

What sets Hotel Rwanda apart is its restraint in depicting violence. Unlike City of God (2002) or The Last King of Scotland (2006), the film suggests horror rather than showing it explicitly. This approach makes the emotional impact even stronger, focusing on faces and reactions rather than graphic violence. The hotel becomes a character itself, much like the factory in Schindler's List (1993), representing both sanctuary and prison. SUBHEAD: Impact on Genocide Cinema and Historical Documentation

movies.slug: The story of UN commander Roméo Dallaire during the Rwandan genocide

sections.content: The success of Hotel Rwanda influenced later genocide films like The Promise (2016) about the Armenian genocide and First They Killed My Father (2017) about the Cambodian genocide. These films share a common thread of focusing on individual acts of heroism against systematic evil, while serving as crucial historical documents. The film's release coincided with other media examining the international community's failure to intervene, including the documentary Shake Hands with the Devil: The Journey of Roméo Dallaire (2004).
